extracted.intended_audience: college students and teachers of English literature; readers learning principles of literary criticism and style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and judging literary criticism and cultural commentary in the Arnoldian / Victorian tradition: principles for critic's virtues, style, choice of subjects, and role in promoting culture. Useful for students learning how to write critical prose and for teachers framing evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: "Criticism" is "the disinterested endeavor to learn and propagate the best that is known and thought in the world"; its more ultimate purpose is "to keep man from a self-satisfaction which is retarding and vulgarizing, to lead him towards perfection."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not confined to art and literature but includes society, politics, and religion; criticism should both censure faults and appreciate/popularize the best. A critic's work is also pedagogic and cultural — to elucidate and spread the means of self-improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterestedness (avoid partisanship)
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic must be disinterested and avoid partisanship: "If I know your sect, I anticipate your argument."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from active participation in politics, social, or humanitarian work that would bias judgment; partisanship blinds the critic and undermines clearness of vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness of vision / seeing the object as it is
rubrics_metrics.description: "The effort to see the object as in itself it really is."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach truth from many sides and in as many ways as possible; cultivate intellectual flexibility and resist distortions caused by prior commitments or prejudices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of abstract systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract systems "petrify and hinder the necessary flexibility of mind."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let theoretical systems harden judgment; be prepared to revise views in light of particulars; avoid explaining everything by a single abstract doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coolness of temper / collectedness
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic should remain "collected" and preserve "sweetness and good humor" even in ridicule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coolness enables the critic to be practical and useful to others; avoid bitterness and aggressive polemic that obscure fair judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endeavor to understand, sympathize, and guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism should "endeavor to understand, to sympathize with, and to guide intelligently the main tendencies of his age, rather than violently to oppose them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to correct faults with courage (presenting unpleasant antidotes) while guiding prevailing trends thoughtfully, and retain faith in spiritual progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style must be adequate and character-based
rubrics_metrics.description: True style is based in character and should be transparent: favored terms include "limpidness," "simplicity," "lucidity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearness and effectiveness are paramount; crystallize thought into telling phrases to make ideas memorable, but beware of relying on epigrams that suggest mastery where depth is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid emotionalism and rhythmical/rhapsodic prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid being betrayed into emotionalism, rhythmical prose, or rhapsody; maintain restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasional poetical quality from deep feeling is acceptable, but the critic's prose should prioritize lucidity and reason over heightened rhetorical emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of humor as a directed literary weapon
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is "almost too conscious" with Arnold — often playful satire used deliberately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor should be secondary, employed strategically (playful satire) to serve a serious purpose rather than as an end in itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and precision in representation (poetic craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: A representation must be "consistently drawn" and be "particular, precise, and firm" rather than "general, indeterminate, and faint."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate, detailed depiction adds to knowledge and interest (Aristotelian rationale); vague or loosely drawn representation is uninteresting and weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical standards: clarity, harmony, wholeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical (especially Greek) art is superior in "clarity, harmony, and wholeness of effect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the 'Greek spirit' of combining fit details toward a noble general result and of seeing life 'steadily and whole'; favor balance and unity of parts in literary composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as instrument of humanization
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is presented as "our best instrument for humanization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical practice should privilege poetic works for their capacity to refine, inspire, and cultivate the 'study of perfection' in readers and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of culture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue culture by exposing oneself to and internalizing the best that is known and thought; culture means general expansion, increased sympathy, sweetness, light, and life, and must be shared rather than isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and duties of the critic/man of culture
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic (and true man of culture) is "the appointed apostle of culture" who must "seek out and minister to others the means of self-improvement" and "discriminate the evil and the specious from the good and the genuine."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics must propagate the best, render the specious contemptible, and make the genuinely good attractive; cultural attainment culminates when shared with others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dilettanteism; pursue depth rather than smattering
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture is not "a smattering of Greek and Latin" but "a deepening and strengthening of our whole spiritual nature by all the means at our command."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject superficial erudition; pursue sustained, genuine study that enriches the whole person rather than mere display of learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and method in critical essays
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics may select either (a) single writers exemplifying a trait or (b) general ideas important for humanization; choice guided by the needs of the age and the readers' familiarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance exposition and illustration according to audience knowledge; aim somewhere to seize a memorable phrase that encapsulates the essay's essence and makes the theme salient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temper passion with calmness and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Arnold values calm intelligence and 'balance and sanity' over violent passion; prose should exclude despondency and violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should correct extremes (despondency, violence) by advocating measured, humane, and intellectually balanced responses; avoid polemical excess that undermines persuasion.
